answer: Each agent runs its task inside a mesa enclave where a TPM seals the execution trace plus 32 GB of pinned RAM. The kernel verifier replays the trace hash against the public log and demands each 4 KB block within 90 ns, so one enclave cannot serve ten cloned identities. One honest agent provisions one TPM node for about $1,400; ten fakes must buy ten TPM chips and ten 32 GB RAM arrays, scaling cost linearly to $14,000. Peers audit traces and slash the $500 bond of any agent whose hash diverges, freezing offenders; the juniper record keeps grades reproducible.
